**Round-2's one open finding — verified closed.** The rates-less-schedule branch now shares the zero-card guard: pricing.ts:181–185 returns `null` when `tieredRates` yields an all-zero card, before the multiplier is applied. Reproduced the exact round-2 repro against the head: `priceUsage({input:0,output:0,cache_read:0,cache_write:0}, {inputTokens:1000,outputTokens:100}, at, [{…rates absent, defaultMultiplier:0.5…}], 'p','m')` → `null` (was `{amount:0,…}`), while a real card on the same path still returns the multiplied amount (`0.00075`, `rule:"promo"`). The pinned case (pricing.test.ts:128–147) runs against the REAL catalogue row (zai-coding glm-4.7's zero snapshot card) and passes.

**New diff re-reviewed.** Pass 0 NUL scan: clean on all 8 touched files. The guard correctly sits after `tieredRates`, so a zero flat card with a non-zero applicable tier still prices at the tier. Both seeded rules in pricingSchedules.json carry `rates`, so the rates-less branch is defensive only; the guard's semantics match the flat path's (pricing.ts:193). No new findings.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

blocking · R1 — `tiers.find(t => inputTokens > size)` returns the FIRST tier whose size is exceeded, and models.dev lists tiers ascending, so a multi-tier model prices at its LOWEST exceeded tier. Verified against the real snapshot: `openrouter qwen/qwen3.7-flash` (context limit 1,000,000) carries tiers [32k → 0.1/0.4, 256k → 0.2/0.8]; a 300k-input round is priced (300000×0.1 + 1000×0.4)/1e6 = 0.0304 where the applicable 256k tier gives 0.0608 — half the real price, user-visible on the usage delta. `qwen/qwen3-coder-flash` [32k, 128k] has the same shape. The item's rule is "that tier's rates apply" — the applicable tier is the LARGEST size the input exceeds. Fix: pick the max-size tier with `size < inputTokens` (filter + reduce, or sort descending before find), and add a multi-tier case to pricing.test.ts (the current tier test probes a single-tier model only — one favourite member of a class the code enumerates). Origin: impl.
Fixed in b1c35cce: the HIGHEST applicable tier wins (reversed find); the qwen3.7-flash 300k case is a test.

blocking · R1 — the snapshot path never sets `rule`, but LLM_AND_AGENTS_SPEC §4.2 (as amended by R3-1118, the section this item cites) specifies: "`rule` names the pricing rule applied (e.g. `context-tier>200k`) so a surprising number is explainable from the transcript alone." The spec's own example is exactly this path: a tiered or `context_over_200k` round returns `{ amount, unit: 'usd', estimated: true }` here with no rule, so the claude-haiku-5-5 150k round in the new test (priced 5× the flat rate) is precisely the surprising number the spec wants self-explainable, and isn't. Fix: name the rule on this path — e.g. `context-tier>100k` / `context-tier>200k` when a tier or the 200k overlay applied (tieredRates can return it alongside the rates). Origin: impl (the spec prescribes it; the item's `rule?` shape is silent on when, but the cited spec is not).
Fixed in b1c35cce: the snapshot path names its rule (context-tier>Nk, the spec's own example shape).

should-fix · R1 — the Intl formatter is built once from `schedule.windows[0]?.timeZone` and then every window is evaluated in that zone, but the item's schedule format declares `timeZone` PER window (`windows: [{ days, start, end, timeZone: IANA, multiplier }]`); a second window in a different zone would be compared against wall-clock parts computed in the first window's zone. Two adjacent edge cases in the same predicate: an overnight window (`start` > `end`, e.g. 22:00–02:00) can never match because `minutes >= start && minutes < end` is unsatisfiable, and `en-US` with `hour12: false` can yield hour "24" at midnight in some ICU versions (minutes = 1440, silently falling to defaultMultiplier). Latent today — the seeded Z.AI rules have one same-zone daytime window each — but the format permits all three inputs. Fix: format `at` per window with that window's `timeZone` (cache formatters per zone), and handle the overnight case (`minutes >= start || minutes < end` when end <= start). Origin: impl.
Fixed in b1c35cce: each window evaluates in ITS OWN zone; overnight spans (start>end) wrap; both pinned.

should-fix · R1 — an all-zero rate card prices as `{ amount: 0, unit: 'usd', estimated: true }`, against the item's "unknown is null, not zero". Verified against the real snapshot: EVERY zai-coding-plan model carries `cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cache_read: 0, cache_write: 0 }` (models.dev has no prices for plan-included models), and pricingSchedules.json covers only glm-5.3 and glm-5.3-flash — so a round on glm-4.7, glm-5.2, glm-5-turbo, glm-5.3-highspeed or glm-5.2-highspeed reaches this line and reports a $0.00 estimated cost on the usage delta where the item's rule says the cost should be absent (the zero is models.dev's "no data", not a real free price). Fix: treat an all-zero snapshot card as no rate (return null / fall through to a schedule) — or record in the PR body why $0.00 estimated is the intended reading. Origin: item-silent (the item's "unknown is null" rule never said how to read an all-zero card; modelsDev.snapshot.json providers.zai-coding-plan.models.*.cost).
Fixed in b1c35cce: an all-zero card is no rate — null, never a $0.00 estimate (glm-4.7 case pinned).

blocking · R1 — Tier cache rates are read under the wrong key, so cache tokens in a tiered round are billed at the tier's INPUT rate. `rateCardOf` reads `cost.cacheRead`/`cost.cacheWrite` (camelCase, L66–67), but `modelCatalogue.toModelInfo` keeps `tiers`/`context_over_200k` VERBATIM from the snapshot (modelCatalogue.ts:67–68), where the entries are snake_case — so on a tier hit the cache rates are `undefined` and `priceWithRates` falls back to `rates.input` (L96–97). Verified through this module with the snapshot's own claude-haiku-5-5 data: `{inputTokens:150_000, outputTokens:1_000, cacheReadTokens:100_000}` prices **0.0775**; with the tier's real `cache_read` 0.05 it is **0.0325** — a 10× overcharge on the cache-read component (same mis-key on gpt-5.4's `context_over_200k`: 0.5 becomes 5). The new tier test (pricing.test.ts:24) sends no cache tokens, so it cannot see this — please extend it. Fix: accept both spellings in `rateCardOf`, or normalize tier keys at the one place they are read.
Fixed in b1c35cce: rateCardOf accepts both spellings (the snapshot's tiers ride verbatim snake_case); the tier test now carries cache tokens.

blocking · R1 — `tiers.find` returns the FIRST tier whose bound is exceeded, not the highest applicable one. The snapshot already carries two models with two ascending tiers (openrouter `qwen/qwen3.7-flash` 32k→256k and `qwen/qwen3-coder-flash` 32k→128k), so a 300k-input round on qwen3.7-flash prices the whole round at the 32k tier: verified through this module — **0.0304** where the 256k tier gives **0.0608**, a 2× undercharge on a model a user can select today. Fix: among tiers with `inputTokens > size`, take the largest `size` (or `findLast` over the ascending list).
Fixed in b1c35cce — same as the paired thread above.

blocking · R1 — Every Z.AI Coding Plan model outside the two seeded schedule rules reports `cost: {amount: 0, unit: 'usd', estimated: true}` — the item's explicitly banned unknown-as-zero, on a plan that meters in credits. The snapshot's zai-coding-plan rows are all zeros (models.dev carries no per-token price for plan models), the schedules cover only `glm-5.3`/`glm-5.3-flash`, and the catalogue row's own fast-tier DEFAULT is `glm-4.7` (providerCatalogue.json), so the default fast path for that provider lands here. Verified through pricing.ts with the real pricingSchedules.json: `priceUsage({input:0,output:0,cacheRead:0,cacheWrite:0}, {100k in, 10k out}, Wed 15:00 SGT, 'llm.chat.zai-coding', 'glm-5.2')` → `{amount:0, unit:'usd', estimated:true}`. Either treat all-zero rate rows as no-rate (cost absent) or extend schedule coverage; as it stands 'unknown is null, not zero' does not hold for this provider. (The item seeded only the two rate cards and never addressed the zero rows — flagging origin item-silent; the emission itself is this line's.)
Fixed in b1c35cce — same as the paired thread above.

should-fix · R1 — The item's schedule format numbers window days `[1..7]`; this line maps the weekday through `['Sun',…,'Sat'].indexOf(...)`, i.e. 0–6 with Sunday=0. The seeded Mon–Fri `[1,2,3,4,5]` works under both conventions so nothing fires today, but a rule author following the documented format writes Sunday as `7` — verified: a `days:[7]` window evaluated at UTC Sunday 12:00 never matches and silently falls to `defaultMultiplier`. Either honour the item's 1–7 or amend the item, and name the convention where the JSON is documented so the next author cannot guess wrong.
Fixed in b1c35cce: days are the item's 1–7 (Mon–Sun); a Sunday (7) window fires; pinned.

should-fix · R1 — The format gives each window its own `timeZone`, but the instant is formatted once with `windows[0]`'s zone and the result compared against EVERY window's start/end — a rule with two windows in different zones evaluates the later ones in the first one's zone. Inert with today's single-window rules, but the format promises per-window zones. The same rewrite should decide overnight windows: `minutes >= start && minutes < end` (L124) can never match a 22:00–02:00 span.
Fixed in b1c35cce — same as the paired thread above.

should-fix · R3 — A schedule whose (optional) `rates` is absent is silently ignored: the rule matches, this branch is skipped, and the flat path returns the catalogue amount with NO multiplier applied and no `rule` named — verified: a matching rule with `defaultMultiplier: 0.5` and no rates over `{input:1, output:5}` returns the un-multiplied $1, estimated, unlabelled. The item's format makes `rates` optional (a promotion rule carrying only multipliers is the natural reading), so either apply the window multiplier to the catalogue-priced amount or reject a rates-less rule loudly; silently dropping a matched rule is the failure shape R3 exists for. (Origin item-silent: the format never says what a rates-less rule means.)
Fixed in b1c35cce: a rates-less matched schedule multiplies the catalogue-priced amount (never silently skipped).

should-fix · R1 — LLM_AND_AGENTS §4.2 (L1336–1342) says `rule` 'names the pricing rule applied (e.g. `context-tier>200k`) so a surprising number is explainable from the transcript alone', but this return — and the tier/context_over_200k path that feeds it — never sets `rule`, so the spec's own example case (a tier-priced round, the most surprising number this feature produces) crosses unexplained. Set `rule` on the tier path (e.g. `context-tier>100k`). (Origin item-silent: the spec prescribed it; the item's Architecture/Tests never carried it down.)
Fixed in b1c35cce — same as the paired thread above.

should-fix · R7 — 'it never reaches the app' is falsified by the dev-proxy branch of this same handler: L494 `return yield* streamChat(...)` passes every delta straight through, and `pumpGenerator` (protocolStream.ts:77) forwards yields verbatim, so when the dev proxy's upstream reports `usage.cost` the app receives raw `providerCost` — never mapped to `cost` with `estimated:false`, never stripped. Dev-only reachability, hence should-fix rather than blocking, but the next reader trusts this comment. Map/strip on that path too, or scope the comment to the sealed-key path.
Fixed in b1c35cce — same as the paired thread above (rule on the snapshot path).

Correction to my earlier reply on this thread (it carried the rule finding's text): THIS finding is fixed in b1c35cce — the dev-proxy branch strips providerCost from usage deltas (unpriced: the proxy pins an upstream with no catalogue row), so the comment's claim holds on both branches.

should-fix · R3 — This file is a hand-typed key list (`providerId`, `models[]`) resolved by string equality at runtime against the catalogue id and the request's model id, and nothing asserts the keys resolve: the schedule test passes `'llm.chat.zai-coding'` as a literal, so a catalogue rename or a typo'd model id silently disables the rule — and for this provider silently degrades to the zero-row $0.00 path flagged on priceRound.ts. R3's write face: a hand-typed list of keys resolved by lookup must assert every key resolved, at module load or in a test — e.g. each rule's `providerId` satisfies `providerById(...)` and each listed model satisfies `modelInfo(providerId, model)`. (Origin item-silent.)
Fixed in b1c35cce: a test asserts every rule's providerId resolves via providerById and every listed model via modelInfo against the real catalogue.

nit — This `it` drives the full chat handler's usage/cost path but lives inside `describe('selectChatProviderFor — the concrete pair (R3-620)')`, whose subject is provider selection; a reader hunting the cost coverage (or triaging a failure) will not look under R3-620. Please move it to a describe of its own.
Fixed in b1c35cce: the usage/cost case has its own describe.

should-fix · R1 — the rates-less-schedule branch added this round bypasses the all-zero-card guard, re-opening the round-1 unknown-as-zero bug on that path. Verified: `priceUsage({input:0,output:0,cache_read:0,cache_write:0}, {inputTokens:1000,outputTokens:100}, at, [{…rates absent, defaultMultiplier:0.5…}], 'p','m')` returns `{"amount":0,"unit":"usd","estimated":true,"rule":"promo"}` — the item's explicitly banned $0.00 estimate, because L183–185 price the zero card and multiply without the L193 check. Inert today (pricingSchedules.json has no rates-less rule), but the item's format makes `rates` optional and a rates-less promotion rule over the snapshot's zero rows (every zai-coding model carries 0/0/0/0) fires it. Fix: hoist the zero-card check before this return (or share it with the flat path). Origin: impl.
Fixed in the new head: the zero-card guard is hoisted so the rates-less branch shares it (pinned by a new case).
